failure_observed: The skill's truth rules (never invent, claim strength <= evidence, cite only verified sources) were enforced by instructions and a WARN-level lint, not by fail-closed checks. Observed in this study's own runs: a README-vs-paper dataset-count conflict resolved only in free text (BEIR v0.2.0 run; the same paper then says 18 datasets in four places and 19 in one), writers inventing a rounded bound absent from the evidence ('all under 350 KB' / 'under 330 KB' when the largest model is 325 KB, MLPerf Tiny, both versions), a garbled reference title silently 'corrected' from model memory (MLPerf Tiny v0.2.0 run, caught only by the writer's own audit), and v0.1.0 runs marking G1/G3 'passed' with no tool output. The user-supplied vNext spec (docs/06_VNEXT_SPEC.md) names ten adversarial cases the guardrail must pass.

components.summary: Evidence conflicts: quantity/run_id keys, automatic same-quantity conflict detection (UNRECONCILED_CONFLICT), documented resolution field, BLOCKED_BY_CONFLICT and CITES_REJECTED_EVIDENCE on claims.

Evidence-conditional language: claim licenses with evidence predicates (validator UNLICENSED_CLAIM), lint UNLICENSED-<type> fail-closed once a claim map uses licenses, WARN for legacy maps; claim basis/status provenance axis; BLOCKED-claim-used.

verify_numbers.py: every draft number traced to evidence values or locator files (rounding, %, K/M/B), derivations only from evidence cited on the same line, p-values never inferred (UNTRACED_PVALUE).
Sources: as_cited + TITLE_REPAIRED_FROM_MEMORY unless verified by lookup.
Fail-closed figure cards (Stage 1 scope for visual cases 4, 6, 7, 8): NO_VALID_VISUAL, VISUAL_BLOCKED, UNTRACED_COMPONENT, BLOCKED_PERMISSION, UNLABELLED_ILLUSTRATION; subset-YAML card reader.

claim_invariance.py (number, scope, strength, dropped/added tags) and effective gate status (PASSED/NOT_RUN/FAILED/STALE/PENDING/UNVERIFIED); with guardrail v0.3, G3 also requires a numbers report and G5 a numbers and an invariance report.

Recursive self-improvement tiers 0-1: rce_diagnostics.py (opt-in, local, content-free run records; recurring-pattern summary) and replay_fixtures.py (fixture library replayed through all checkers, machine log).
Within-draft count consistency (lint INCONSISTENT-COUNT), excluding explained subsets.

change.summary: Builds on the v0.2.0 candidate (its attribution and executable-gate code is kept; v0.2.0 itself was rejected on reader outcomes, not on tool correctness). All additions are backward compatible: artifacts without the new fields validate exactly as before; the new ERROR-level rules switch on only when a project adopts them (claim-map `licenses`, state.json `guardrail: v0.3`). No existing test changed.

expected_improvement: Tool-level (acceptance criterion of spec Stage 1): all ten adversarial cases behave as specified, with machine logs and no invented evidence -- met, 16/16 failure fixtures and 9/9 controls. Paper-level: fewer untraceable numbers, silent conflict resolutions and repaired titles reaching a draft. Reader-level: NOT claimed. These are checkers, so the offline replay gate is the right acceptance test for them; whether they change reader reconstruction is unmeasured and needs a seeded live A/B (RECOMMENDED_NEXT_VERSION Part A.2).
possible_regressions: Lint noise: UNLICENSED-* WARNs on legacy drafts (e.g. 'generalize' in a zero-shot benchmark paper is correct but unlicensed in a legacy claim map).
Writer burden: licenses, quantities and resolutions add bookkeeping; a writer may downgrade correct wording rather than record the license.
verify_numbers false alarms when a number appears in the source in another format (e.g. 32K vs 32,000 now handled; unicode minus or table damage may not be).
verify_numbers misses fabricated numbers that coincide with any number in a dense source (5/40 in the probe).
Count-consistency heuristics are English-only and pattern-based.
Scope/strength drift detection is lexical: paraphrases that change scope without trigger words pass.
